mcqs.question: The Election Commission of India was expected to announce the pan-India Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls on which date, with the first phase covering which group of States and Union Territories?
options: 27 October 2025; 10–15 States, including Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry
22–23 October 2025; 12 States and Union Territories, including Bihar
10 July 2025; all States and Union Territories simultaneously
6 November 2025; only the 2026 poll States and Union Territories
mcqs.explanation: The ECI was to announce the pan-India SIR on 27 October 2025, with the first phase covering 10–15 States and Union Territories, including Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry. The other options substitute dates or coverage details from different parts of the electoral-roll revision discussion.

mcqs.question: Which of the following set of digital tools was identified in connection with the pan-India Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls?
options: Voter Helpline App, NVSP and ERONet
NJDG, ICJS and Case Information System
mcqs.explanation: The tools associated with the electoral-roll revision are the Voter Helpline App, NVSP and ERONet. NJDG, ICJS, Case Information System and virtual courts belong to the e-Courts or judicial-digitalisation context.

mcqs.question: What is the full form of SVEEP in the context of electoral participation?
options: Systematic Voters’ Education and Electoral Participation
Special Verification of Electoral Entries and Polling
Statewide Voter Enrolment and Election Programme
System for Voter Enumeration, Examination and Protection
mcqs.explanation: SVEEP stands for Systematic Voters’ Education and Electoral Participation. The other expansions are not the name of the voter-education and participation initiative.

mcqs.question: What did the Supreme Court’s order of 10 July 2025 do in relation to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls?
options: It framed whether the ECI could conduct SIR, did not stay the Bihar SIR, and ordered draft-roll publication and Aadhaar inclusion
It stayed the Bihar SIR and prohibited Aadhaar from being included in the electoral-roll process
It transferred the SIR entirely to State Election Commissions and cancelled draft-roll publication
It held that the ECI could conduct SIR only after approval by the Union Cabinet
mcqs.explanation: The 10 July 2025 order framed the question of whether the ECI could conduct SIR, did not stay the Bihar SIR, and ordered draft-roll publication and Aadhaar inclusion. The other options reverse or alter these directions.

mcqs.question: Which group comprised the petitioners’ counsel in the Supreme Court proceedings concerning the ECI’s powers over electoral-roll revision?
options: Prashant Bhushan, Vrinda Grover and Neha Rathi
Quraishi, Anuradha Talwar and B.V. Nagarathna
Prashant Bhushan, Mohinder Singh Gill and Lal Babu Hussain
Vrinda Grover, Neha Rathi and the Chief Election Commissioner
mcqs.explanation: The petitioners’ counsel were Prashant Bhushan, Vrinda Grover and Neha Rathi. The other options mix counsel with judges, litigants, or names associated with other parts of the issue.

mcqs.question:
With reference to citizenship requirements in electoral registration, consider the following statements:
1. Article 326 embodies universal adult suffrage, under which only citizens can vote.
2. Section 16 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides that only citizens can be registered.
3. Section 16 permits non-citizens to be registered if they satisfy the age requirement.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Article 326 concerns universal adult suffrage limited to citizens, and Section 16 permits registration only of citizens. Statement 3 is false because the citizenship requirement is not removed by satisfying the age requirement.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Election Commission of India.

List-I
(a) Article 324(2)
(b) Selection committee under the 2023 arrangement

List-II
(i) Prime Minister as chair, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
(ii) Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners as the President decides
(iii) Six years or 65 years, with the CEC removable like a Supreme Court judge
(iv) Advice to the President and Governors on disqualification under Articles 103 and 192
mcqs.explanation: Article 324(2) concerns the CEC and ECs as the President decides, while the 2023 selection committee consists of the Prime Minister as chair, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. Therefore, the correct pairs are a-ii and b-i.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The tenure of the Election Commissioners is six years or until attaining 65 years, and the CEC is removable only like a Supreme Court judge.
Statement B: The ECI advises the President and Governors on disqualification under Articles 103 and 192.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The stated tenure is six years or 65 years, the CEC has the specified removal protection, and the ECI advises the President and Governors under Articles 103 and 192 on disqualification.

mcqs.question:
Match the phases of the e-Courts Project with their principal features.

List-I
(a) Phase I, 2010–2015
(b) Phase II, 2015–2023

List-II
(i) e-filing, e-payment, NJDG and virtual courts
(ii) Case Information System and computerisation of more than 14,000 courts
(iii) Integration with ICJS and the National Policy and Action Plan for ICT in Indian Judiciary
(iv) Digitisation of 3,108 crore documents and creation of 25 PB cloud capacity
mcqs.explanation: Phase I, from 2010 to 2015, involved the Case Information System and computerisation of more than 14,000 courts. Phase II, from 2015 to 2023, introduced e-filing, e-payment, NJDG and virtual courts.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the e-Courts Project:
1. Its origin lies in the National Policy and Action Plan for ICT in Indian Judiciary, 2005, of the Supreme Court e-Committee.
2. It is implemented by the Department of Justice with NIC under NeGP.
3. Its integration with ICJS is limited to courts and excludes police, jails and forensics.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the project originated in the 2005 National Policy and Action Plan, and is implemented by the Department of Justice with NIC under NeGP. Statement 3 is false because ICJS integration covers courts, police, jails and forensics.

mcqs.question: In the dispute over resumption of MGNREGS work in West Bengal, what was the approximate number of workers affected after funds were stopped on 21 December 2021 and work permits were halted by March 2022?
mcqs.explanation: About 25 million workers were affected. The other figures belong to unrelated electoral-roll or e-Courts details and are not the number of workers affected in West Bengal.

mcqs.question: Who was the petitioner in the MGNREGS case concerning West Bengal, and who was the convenor of NREGA Sangharsh Morcha?
options: Paschim Banga Khet Majoor Samity; Anuradha Talwar
NREGA Sangharsh Morcha; Paschim Banga Khet Majoor Samity
The Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister; Anuradha Talwar
mcqs.explanation: Paschim Banga Khet Majoor Samity was the petitioner, and Anuradha Talwar was the convenor of NREGA Sangharsh Morcha. The other options reverse the roles or introduce a person from a different issue.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
1. The Act was enacted in 2005, the scheme began in 2006, and it guarantees 100 days of wage work per rural household.
2. The Centre bears 100% of wages, while material and administrative costs are shared in the ratio of 75:25.
3. Unemployment allowance becomes payable only when work is not provided within 30 days.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MGNREGA was enacted in 2005, implemented as a scheme from 2006, guarantees 100 days of work, and has the stated funding pattern. Statement 3 is false because unemployment allowance is payable when work is not provided within 15 days; social audit is conducted by the Gram Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Match the following persons, institutions or States with the associated development in the debate on freebies and welfare.

List-I
(a) Former CEC Quraishi
(b) Supreme Court, November 2023
(c) Punjab
(d) Rajasthan

List-II
(i) Plea admitted to treat freebies as a corrupt practice; Justice B.V. Nagarathna
(ii) 300 free units and debt-to-GSDP of 47.2% in 2023–24
(iii) ₹56,000 crore in pre-poll schemes
(iv) Argument concerning the “weaponisation of welfare”
mcqs.explanation: Quraishi advanced the argument about the “weaponisation of welfare”; the Supreme Court in November 2023 admitted the plea concerning freebies as a corrupt practice, with Justice B.V. Nagarathna noted; Punjab was associated with 300 free units and a 47.2% debt-to-GSDP ratio; and Rajasthan had ₹56,000 crore in pre-poll schemes. Hence, the correct pairs are a-iv, b-i, c-ii and d-iii.
